10 Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. (Matthew 5:10 KJV

This is part of the Sermon on the Mount that Jesus gave. Many Christians think that if they are doing God’s will, they will not suffer persecution, but that is not so. All who live the Christian life will suffer persecution (John 15:18-20, Philippians 1:29-30). If you are not suffering any persecution then you are not living a Christian life (2 Timothy 3:12). This persecution comes from Satan, and is to take away God’s Word (Mark 4:16-17), and take our eyes off Jesus (Hebrews 12:1-3). One of the worst kinds of persecution is what people say about us (Matthew 5:11-12).

It helps to realize that the persecution is not at you, but at Christ who is living through you (Acts 9:4). Many places in the Bible we are told to rejoice during persecution, as our reward in heaven will more then offset our trials on earth. We need to have the strong faith and perseverance to withstand all the persecution that Satan can throw at us, and still remain strong in our walk with the Lord. That rubs Satan’s nose in it more than anything. Just remember that we have to work out our salvation (Philippians 2:12), by obeying Jesus (Hebrews 5:9), and keeping our faith strong in Him. Thank you Jesus for our salvation!
